title: The instructions after amrit
hook: the initiated are told the banis, the five Ks and the four things to avoid

segments.voice: Yesterday, who gives amrit: five Sikhs who have taken it themselves, and a sixth attending the Granth. Your line was the five give. What did you pass on, and to whom? Day one thousand two hundred seventy-three.

The amrit has been drunk. It has been sprinkled on the eyes and the hair. The words have been called out and answered. From the outside, this would look like the end of the ceremony. And still nobody leaves. One of the five turns to the newly initiated and starts to speak, slowly, the way you'd give directions to someone who has to remember them without a map. Before anyone walks out of that quiet room, the promise gets spelled out, piece by piece, out loud. Nothing is left in small print. Today: the instructions after amrit.
screen: `THE AMRIT HAS BEEN GIVEN.` → `AND STILL NOBODY LEAVES.` → `THE PROMISE, SPELLED OUT.`

segments.voice: The Sikh Rehat Maryada sets out what is said, and here it is in paraphrase, in four parts. First, a new family. The initiated are told that from today they are born into the Guru's household. Guru Gobind Singh is their spiritual father, Mata Sahib Kaur their spiritual mother, and Anandpur their home. Whatever caste or clan they came from is left behind; they are now one family with every other Sikh of the Khalsa. Second, the daily banis. Morning, evening and night, the code names what is to be recited, prayers this path walked through not long ago: Japji and Jaap among them at dawn, Rehras at evening, Kirtan Sohila before sleep. Third, the five Ks: kesh, uncut hair; kangha, the comb; kara, the steel bracelet; kachhera, the shorts worn underneath; and kirpan, the sword. Each is to be kept on the body. Fourth, the things to avoid. The code calls them kurahits and names four: dishonoring the hair by cutting it; eating the meat of an animal killed in the ritual way the code calls kutha; sexual contact with anyone other than one's spouse; and using tobacco. The code adds that someone who commits one of these must come back and take amrit again. Look at the order. Family comes first, before any rule. A person is told who they now belong to, and only then what they now do. The rules hang on the relationship, not the other way round. And look at the setting. All of this is said aloud, in the Guru's presence, in front of the five. Nobody can say later that they weren't told. That's the point of today's line. Not a vague feeling of commitment, but what is promised: specific, spoken, and heard.
screen: `A NEW FAMILY: THE GURU'S HOUSEHOLD.` · `THE DAILY BANIS.` · `THE FIVE Ks, KEPT ON THE BODY.` · `FOUR THINGS TO AVOID.` · then, large: `WHAT IS PROMISED.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: write down one promise. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one promise you have already made: to a person, to yourself, to God if you pray. Not a new one; one that already exists. Now find the plain words for it. Short enough to fit on a sticky note. If you have paper, write it. If not, say it once in your head, slowly, as if someone were listening for every word. Then sit with it until the bell, and notice whether the plain version feels heavier or lighter than the vague one. The bell holds the time.
The instructions after amrit. The new Khalsa family, the daily banis, the five Ks and the four things to avoid, spoken aloud before anyone leaves. Today's word.
Your line: what is promised. Today, when you agree to something, say back exactly what you've agreed to, in one plain sentence, so both of you hear it. Day one thousand two hundred seventy-three.

notes: All four parts (spiritual father Guru Gobind Singh, mother Mata Sahib Kaur, home Anandpur; the daily banis; the five Ks; the four kurahits and re-initiation for committing one) are paraphrased from the Sikh Rehat Maryada's account of what is told to the initiated. Please confirm the paraphrase, especially the wording of the kurahits.
The code also names Kesgarh Sahib as the initiated's birthplace; day 1280 picks that up, so today mentions Anandpur only. Please confirm.

The daily banis are given in brief ('Japji and Jaap among them'); day 1253 covered the list in full. The code's further instruction about not associating with certain groups is left out for length; please advise whether it should be included.
'Kirtan Sohila before sleep' and 'Rehras at evening' follow the code's daily schedule; please confirm.
